(i) intrinsic motivation can be defined in terms of a machine learning framework, namely, reinforcement learning, (ii) intrinsic motivation can lead to more efficient learning in reinforcement learning, and (iii) intrinsic motivation can help to solve a fundamental challenge for reinforcement learning, namely, how to explore when the environment is not fully known and there is a trade-off between exploitation and exploration

(1) intrinsic motivation, as it is understood in animal learning theory, can be formalized in terms of reinforcement learning; (2) the resulting reinforcement learning framework is a generalization of classical animal learning theory; (3) intrinsic motivation can be implemented in terms of the temporal-difference (TD) learning algorithm; (4) intrinsic motivation can help an agent solve problems that are otherwise intractable; (5) intrinsic motivation is not only a useful tool for the design of reinforcement learning
(a) intrinsic motivation is a natural and important aspect of reinforcement learning, and (b) the intrinsic reward hypothesis is a viable and useful principle of intrinsic motivation.
